name: 1824 Prairie Avenue (the Pomeroy/Marsh house): the brick stable on the alley, K12

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Robinson's 1886 plate 10, which dates the 1600 and 1700 blocks' stables, stops at 18th Street, and nothing else read dates this one, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (west) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 28 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_28.jpg) at pixel (574.90, 2658.08): the alley wall's line, read by median darkness profile at rows 2510-2550, 2640-2680 and 2780-2820 (575.83, 574.78, 573.96; the raster leans about 0.6 degrees, so the line is fitted through the three), halfway between the building's north and south wall lines (2483.98 and 2832.18). Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json): local E 1338.811, N -3292.139, 1.56 m north of the middle of parcel prairie_1824's rear line (the building stands against the lot's north line and leaves a 3 m yard at its south end), plus the datum origin. The bearing is the parcel's own (its north and south lines both run at 0.627 degrees north of east), so the building's ends lie along the lot lines.
placement.symbolic_location: 1824 S. Prairie Avenue: west side of Prairie between 18th and 20th Streets, the lot directly south of 1816, parcel prairie_1824 (data/street_grid/1904.json); on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the east line of the alley between Indiana and Prairie.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 574.90 at its middle row) to its east wall line (785.04; read at rows 2510-2550, 2640-2680 and 2780-2820: 786.36, 785.28, 783.30, so 210.5, 210.5 and 209.3 pixels from the alley line) and from its north wall line (row 2483.98, the line it shares with 1816's building, which the sheet draws once) to its south one (2832.18): about 210.1 by 348.2 pixels at the sheet's 0.050558 m a pixel, 10.62 m deep by 17.60 m along the alley. South of it the sheet leaves an open strip about 3 m wide to the 1824/1828 lot line (row 2893) and 1828's own building beyond (row 2913). The sheet's fire-wall sign stands at the alley end of both its north and its south wall, so both ends are built as party walls; their returns stand 0.5 m past the eaves, which is the kit's and not the sheet's. The north party wall stands inside this outline, back to back with 1816's own south party wall on the same line, as 1626's and 1628's do on sheet 20.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-west corner: two storeys. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under the kit's 40-degree roof (4.5 m from eave to ridge over the 10.62 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. The sheet gives this building 2 where it gives 1816's 2½, so the roof space is left as the kit builds it, with no dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12' over '8' (inches: the lower storey's and the upper's) inside its north and south walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the one window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1824-stable-1935. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall, the same sign 1816's alley wall carries twice (a cross with a dot for each storey): 8.34 m from the north wall (row 2648.9). The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it (s counts from the north party wall's inner face, 0.33 m in). The rest of the alley wall is the kit's laid out for a building this long (17.6 m, as 1816's 22.4 m is laid out): two carriage bays 3.0 m clear, the loft hatch and hoist over the northern one and a loft sash over the other, a man door between the northern bay and the mark, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard where the walk to the house meets it, and three stable sash with loft sash over them. Both ends are party walls (the sheet's fire-wall signs), so there is no open gable. The kit's 40-degree gable runs its ridge along the alley. The workyard is paved from the yard door 9.08 m east to the west wall of the house's brick body (sheet column 964.6, rows 2585.7-2799.5), the walk on that wall's middle, 1.75 m south of the building's. A small ring the sheet draws inside the building's south-west corner (about column 590, row 2817) is not read and builds nothing.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED except where the window mark places a sash. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 28 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a brick building two storeys high on the alley behind 1824 and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is a 1911 use and is not read as the 1904 one (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11): the T-1841 sheet census (row s28-1824-rear) backcasts the building to 1904 and reconstructs its use as the house's stable and coach house, and this record builds it as that, two carriage bays, a loft hatch with its hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-1935 refines the district draft (T-2329) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the second of the package's seven alley buildings on the west side of Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th, after 1816's next door, and the third K12 coach house on sheet 28. The sheet census (census row s28-1824-rear, trace s28fp-1824-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 28 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle, which had stood it 9.75 m deep and 17.25 m along the alley, 0.75 m in from the alley line: the sheet draws one plain rectangle on the alley line, 10.62 m deep and 17.60 m along it, its north wall on the line it shares with 1816's building. Robinson's 1886 atlas (plate 10) stops at 18th Street, so nothing read here dates the building before 1911. The one picture the T-1935 image gate names for it (Clark's c. 1905 street view north from 1936) shows the house fronts on Prairie Avenue and not the alley.
